matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction). The numeric imbalance tells you what change is needed (e.g., +5, –5, +2, –1). This guides which transformation to try.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of every puzzle, after reading the equation.
matchstick.example: Skipping the numeric check and moving a stick arbitrarily, leading to a numerically false equation.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly +5 and a V appears on the side that needs to increase, move a diagonal stick onto that V so it becomes an X (adds 5). Ensure the source stick’s original symbol stays valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side that must increase is short by 5 and contains a V.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a numeral that cannot lose it (e.g., from an X that would become invalid) or forgetting to keep the source symbol valid.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from any numeral that already contains at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I (e.g., after a V to make VI, or before a V to make IV). The source numeral must remain a valid Roman numeral after losing the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is a multiple of 1 and an I‑stick is available on a numeral that can spare it.
matchstick.example: Taking an I from a solitary I (leaving it empty) or creating an invalid numeral like ‘VV’.

matchstick.title: Reposition I relative to V to change IV↔VI
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains the pattern IV (or VI) and the numeric imbalance is 2, move the I‑stick from before the V to after it (or vice‑versa). This swaps 4↔6, changing the side’s value by 2 while keeping both numerals valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and a V with an adjacent I appears on the side that needs to change.
matchstick.example: Moving the I to a place where it no longer forms a proper IV/VI, producing an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly –5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, move one of its diagonal sticks onto a V (or elsewhere) so the X becomes a V (value drops from 10 to 5). Ensure the destination symbol stays valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a side is too large by 5 and contains an X.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals to the minus (or vice‑versa) to turn ‘=’ into ‘‑’ and ‘‑’ into ‘=’. The remaining symbols must stay valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both ‘‑’ and ‘=’ and the numeric imbalance suggests a change of operator.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from ‘=’ and leaving only one line, which destroys the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present and the numeric imbalance is ±1, moving its vertical stick away turns ‘+’ into ‘‑’ and adds an I‑stick to a numeral (increasing that side by 1). Ensure the plus becomes a valid minus and the destination numeral can accept the new I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 1 (or –1) and a ‘+’ appears.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from ‘+’ but not placing the I anywhere, leaving a stray stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When you relocate a stick from the equality sign, ensure that at least one horizontal remains so the symbol stays a valid ‘=’. The moved stick must be used elsewhere to keep the total stick count unchanged.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider taking a stick from ‘=’.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal from ‘=’ and leaving only a single line, which becomes a minus sign and eliminates the equality.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI↔IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains the pattern ‘XI’, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to ‘IX’, decreasing the value by 2. The reverse move (IX→XI) increases by 2. Both resulting numerals must be valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and a numeral with ‘XI’ or ‘IX’ appears on the side that needs to change.
matchstick.example: Moving the I to a position that no longer forms a proper ‘IX’ or ‘XI’, yielding an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, you can move a vertical I‑stick from any numeral on the larger side to any numeral on the smaller side, adjusting the totals by ±2 while keeping all numerals valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and an I‑stick is available on the side that is too large.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a solitary I, leaving it empty, or creating an invalid numeral on the receiving side.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as removable without checking whether the source numeral still conforms to Roman‑numeral rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick, verify that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move and neglects the overall syntactic validity of the resulting expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the move, check that every symbol (numerals and operators) is a recognized Roman numeral or operator and that the equation contains exactly one ‘=’ and proper operands.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid ‘=’ sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any horizontal can be taken from ‘=’ without considering that at least two horizontals are required for a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from ‘=’, ensure at least one horizontal remains; otherwise, do not take from ‘=’.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after producing a syntactically correct expression and does not recompute the arithmetic to confirm correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the numeric values of both sides after the move and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes describes a multi‑step alteration or forgets that only one stick may be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks you move; ensure exactly one stick is taken from one place and placed elsewhere.
